top_choice_rationale: P004 (Car and Parrinello) is a single, fully mature invention from 1985: ab initio molecular dynamics, with nuclei moving on electronic ground-state surfaces computed on the fly. It has four decades of independent validation and broad use across liquids, solids, interfaces and reactive chemistry. Allocation is exact, with one paper and two names, so no one is trimmed. The 'already served' objection from the 1998 DFT and 2013 multiscale prizes is a real one, but ab initio dynamics is a distinct capability. P002 (C-N cross-coupling) comes next for maturity and clean attribution, then P001 (protein degradation), whose laureate allocation and the question of Ciulli, Crews and Deshaies versus the cereblon work remain contested. P003 pairs two unrelated parts and is the weakest allocation of the four. I rank it above no award because each part is substantial.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Aqvist's own work is in biomolecular simulation, and his postdoc with Arieh Warshel is a loose methodological connection to the computational field, but neither Car nor Parrinello is a listed collaborator
